1.title: Resources, Data Sources and References
1.text: Welcome to Module five: Resources, Data Sources and References. It covers the exam area four. Terraform configuration. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. four A Use and differentiate resource and data blocks. four B Refer to resource attributes and create cross-resource references. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: four. Terraform configuration. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: Resource blocks
1.text: Resource blocks. A resource block declares infrastructure that Terraform manages: it creates, updates and destroys it. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Resource blocks, continued
1.text: Resource blocks. resource. The block type. aws instance. The resource type: provider name plus kind of object. web. The local name, unique within the module for that type. Body. Arguments (inputs you set). The address of this resource is aws instance dot web. After creation it also has attributes (outputs such as an I D) that you can read but not set.

1.title: Data sources
1.text: Data sources. A data source reads information that already exists (outside this configuration or from another configuration). It does not create anything.

1.title: Data sources, continued
1.text: Data sources. The figure shows this: A resource is created and managed; a data source is only read.

1.title: Data sources, continued
1.text: Data sources. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Data sources, continued
1.text: Data sources. Keyword. Resource block: resource. Data block: data. Purpose. Resource block: Manage (create, update, destroy). Data block: Read existing information. In state. Resource block: Yes, managed. Data block: Yes, as read-only. Reference. Resource block: aws instance dot web dot id. Data block: data dot aws ami dot ubuntu dot id. Plan symbol. Resource block: plus, about, -. Data block: (read). Exam tip: resource creates and manages; data only reads. Data references start with data.

1.title: References and implicit dependencies
1.text: References and implicit dependencies. You refer to other objects by their address and Terraform builds a dependency graph from those references. aws instance dot web dot id. The id attribute of a resource. data dot aws ami dot ubuntu dot id. The id of a data source. var dot region. An input variable. local dot name. A local value. module dot network dot vpc id. An output of a child module. each dot key, each dot value, count dot index. Values inside for each and count. self. The resource itself (in some blocks).

1.title: References and implicit dependencies, continued
1.text: References and implicit dependencies. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: References and implicit dependencies, continued
1.text: References and implicit dependencies. Because aws instance dot web uses aws subnet dot main dot id, Terraform creates the subnet first. This is an implicit dependency. (Module eight covers explicit dependencies.). Exam tip: A reference creates an implicit dependency, so order follows from the references, not from the order in the file.

1.title: Meta-arguments you may meet
1.text: Meta-arguments you may meet. count. Create several copies by number. for each. Create several copies from a map or set. provider. Choose a provider configuration (alias). depends on. Explicit dependency. lifecycle. Lifecycle rules. Exam tip: Look at the prefix: data. is read-only, var. is an input, local. is a named expression, module. is a child output.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A configuration must look up the I D of an existing network that another team created. Which block type should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A data block. A data block reads information about existing objects without managing them.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. How is the id attribute of a resource named aws instance.web referenced in other blocks? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: aws instance.web.id. A resource attribute is referenced as T Y P E.N A M E.A T T R I B U T E.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. How is an attribute of a data source named aws ami.ubuntu referenced? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: data.aws ami.ubuntu.id. Data source references start with the data prefix.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A resource references an attribute of a second resource. What does Terraform do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: It creates the second resource first because of the implicit dependency. A reference creates an implicit dependency, so the referenced resource is created first.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. What is the local name in the block resource "aws instance" "web"? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: web. The second label, web, is the local name used in the address aws instance.web.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. In a plan, how is the reading of a data source usually shown? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: With the symbol for reading a data source. Reading a data source is shown with the read symbol, which differs from create, update and destroy.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which block manages infrastructure? Answer: The resource block. Question two. Which block only reads existing information? Answer: The data block. Question three. What is the address of resource "aws instance" "web"? Answer: aws instance.web.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What starts a data source reference? Answer: data. Question five. What does a reference create between resources? Answer: An implicit dependency. Question six. Name two meta-arguments. Answer: For example count and for each.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. resource: T Y P E and local name; manages; address T Y P E.N A M E. data: reads existing objects; reference starts with data. References: var., local., module., each., count.; create implicit dependencies. Meta-arguments: count, for each, provider, depends on, lifecycle.
